children.value: In simple sample spaces, one way to calculate the probability of an event involves counting the number of outcomes in the event and the number of outcomes in the sample space. This section presents some common methods for counting the number of outcomes in a set. These methods rely on special structure that exists in many common experiments, namely, that each outcome consists of several parts and that it is relatively easy to count how many possibilities there are for each of the parts.
